newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia lost $8 mln in wheat malpractices - agency.
newsitem.headline: Croatia lost $8 mln in wheat malpractices - agency.

text.p: Croatia is estimated to have lost 49.3 million kuna ($8.2 million) in the past two years to malpractices in the national commodity reserves, the state news agency Hina reported on Friday.

It said a parliamentary commission set up several months ago to investigate the so-called "wheat affair" had come up with evidence of 50 people being involved in the sale of wheat from reserves and other puhishable acts.
Overall, the state reserve board had intervened on the market too frequently and without sound reason, commission president Vladimir Seks was quoted as saying.
He said stocks in 1995 and 1996 continually showed surpluses of wheat when they did not exist. This wheat was sold in Croatia or exported.
This often benefited private interests of commodity traders linked to the reserve board more than itself, he added.
The government has since replaced the head of the board, while also trying to reorganise it and make it directly responsible to the economy ministry.
The reserve board was previously a semi-autonomous body which anwered only to parliament.
